correctness.rationale: Precisely two labelled twelve-vertex graphs and a strict-neighbor binary majority update, including incumbent tie on the quartic graph, are specified. Every one of the 4096 states per graph was checked by two separately constructed successor arrays and independent classification algorithms: forward first-repetition propagation (Python) and indegree-zero peeling plus reverse distance propagation (C++). They agree on all first-entry period table cells: truncated tetrahedron period-one (16,238,468,720,216,72), period-two (478,1264,528,96), and cuboctahedron period-one (146,1606,1200,1008,96), period-two (40). These cover exactly 4096 states per graph. The cuboctahedral period-two basin contains no entries after zero; hence all 20 cycles have only their two configurations as preimages. Automorphism groups of sizes 24 and 48 are reconstructed and checked, and both orbit enumeration and Burnside confirm geometric classes (5,26) and (14,3). Exact witness states 310 and 348 attain entry times five and four. Full deterministic executable programs and fixed reference census replayed successfully; no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the paired exact first-entry/attraction-basin contrast and particularly the isolated cuboctahedral two-cycles versus 1888 nonperiodic two-cycle-basin states on the truncated tetrahedron. The classical eventual-period-two theorem does not provide any of these basin populations. A prior general half-factor theorem implies recurrent counts for the cuboctahedron as a special case; those numbers are acknowledged as context and not independently claimed novel. Its premises and conclusion concern recurrent states and give neither the size nor the absence of transient preimages. The truncated tetrahedron has a line-graph representation with degree-parity-mixed base edges, outside the prior theorem hypothesis. Published full results on the same Archimedean pair concern higher-independence homotopy and three-state excitation, not binary majority. Exact-number, graph-name, alias and transient-isolation searches found no equivalently covering claim. An unindexed older full finite graph census remains the specific uncertainty.

value.rationale: The two twelve-vertex Archimedean solids are canonical vertex-transitive graphs. A mathematically natural comparison of the same binary majority update on these two compact, symmetric graph geometries yields a strong qualitative separation not reflected in general period-one-or-two theorems: cuboctahedral two-cycles are completely isolated with only 40 eventually oscillatory states, while 2366 truncated-tetrahedron states oscillate eventually, including 1888 initially transient ones. Exact first-entry histograms, sharp times five versus four, and complete temporal/geometric orbit populations provide reusable benchmark cases for the distinction between periodic-state classification and attraction basins. This precise finite comparison is substantive even without an infinite-family consequence; no claim of a universal edge-addition principle is made.
